newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK blocks merger of London casino operators.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK blocks merger of London casino operators.

text.p: The British government on Tuesday sank the plans of casino operator London Clubs International (LCI) to acquire British rival Capital Corporation Plc .
Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett ruled the plan would be against the public interest since it would give LCI an 80 percent share of business in London's lucrative up-market casinos.
LCI tabled a 190 million pound ($310 million) hostile bid for Capital earlier this year but the bid lapsed after the previous Conservative government referred it to competition authorities in April.

Regulatory clearance would have paved the way for a fresh bid by LCI for Capital, which operates Crockfords and the Colony Club for high rollers in the swish Mayfair area of central London. The ruling sent shares in both companies lower, LCI losing 15.5p to 387p while Capital fell some 10 percent, shedding 18.5p to 165.5p.

LCI chief executive Alan Goodenough said the ruling was "disappointing" and based on "flawed logic". He argued that strict regulation made it impossible for a company to exploit a dominant market position.
Capital welcomed the decision, which it said removed an unwanted distraction.

Goodenough said LCI would now seek to accelerate its expansion overseas. Foreign earnings account for only 10 percent of annual turnover of around 180 million pounds but LCI is aiming for a 50/50 split within the next two or three years.
It already has casinos in France, Lebanon and Egypt in addition to its seven in London. It is set to open in Las Vegas and is pitching for two licences in South Africa and another at Niagara Falls.

Goodenough won support from stock broker Dresdner Kleinwort Benson which issued a research note highlighting LCI's earnings potential and arguing that the Capital deal was not crucial to long-term success.

The broker said speculation was likely to return to British leisure companies Ladbroke Group Plc and Rank Group Plc or Mirage Resorts of the U.S. as possible suitors for Capital Corp. But it noted they too might fall foul of the UK competition authorities. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
